Now that said I’m curious what the actual levels are and what the safety standards are set at.

He is using a field strength meter (this one).

The unit he is measuring is mV/m (millivolts per meter). This unit is called field strength. Normally what you want to look at is power density, and the unit for that is mW/m2 (milliwatts per square meter). There is a mathematical conversion formula between the two, so knowing one you can calculate the other, but the reason to prefer power density is that most microwave safety guidelines are stated using that.

Not sure why Steele is using field strength. I think it is not a good idea to create more confusion, but some people get stuck with their preferred unit, and it is difficult to switch after you get a sense of the ranges of one unit in relation to health effects. The conversion formula from one unit to another is not linear, so it is not easy to switch once you get accustomed to either one.

In the first video he said the numbers popped to 4000 mV/m. This is equivalent to about 40 mW/m2. This is quite a high reading, but still within US FCC and EU ICNIRP guidelines. That does not mean these readings are safe, and in fact I would personally not want to be in such a field for prolonged periods of time. The reason is that the international guidelines are set based on wireless industry requirements, and not real biological safety.

To give you some idea of where on the scale of exposure this hits, you can look at the graph below which shows reported biological effects plotted in relation to power density (vertical scale on the left).

https://files.catbox.moe/5pz32i.png

As you can see 40mW/m2 is on the upper end of the graph. For comparison, in my own bedroom I measure 0.002 mW/m2, which I consider borderline acceptable for sleeping. I would personally prefer it a bit lower for good safety, but it is still way below what most people in urban environments sleep in. The reason why you want to focus on the bedroom first, is because sleep is the most important time for cellular repair and regeneration. Not only do you want low light and low noise, but you also want to minimize RF exposure during this time.

There is a lot more to talk about on this subject, but hopefully this gives you some idea of what these numbers mean.
